impact_scope.description: JPEG scan completion now increments internal scan_count; decode_frame detects completed scans and performs swizzling there, while restart_frame resets scan_count. This changes internal handling of the existing decode-frame/restart-frame protocol without adding a public API, format, configuration, or caller argument.

evidence: In S0, decoder.restart_frame already existed with the same caller-supplied index and io_position and call-sequence requirements.
H0 only initializes the decoder and invokes decode_image_config, decode_frame_config, and decode_frame through fuzz_image_decoder; it never invokes restart_frame.
H0 does exercise ordinary decode_frame processing, including input-selected JPEG scan structure, so the relocated scan swizzling does not itself require a new harness action.
In S1, H0 still never invokes decoder.restart_frame, so the same existing restart protocol remains unexercised.
The added scan_count reset is internal to restart_frame; its public signature, arguments, and call-order eligibility are unchanged from S0.
H0 continues to exercise decode_frame with caller-controlled JPEG bytes, and scan_count plus the moved swizzling are managed internally by the decoder.

new_harness_obligation.description: The commit introduces no new entry point, caller-supplied argument or buffer, configuration action, compile-time enablement, input format, or call-order transition. Exercising restart_frame was already an optional same-scope harness action in S0, and scan_count requires no caller control.
evidence: decoder.decode_frame and decoder.restart_frame retain their existing public signatures.
scan_count is a private decoder field updated by decode_sos and reset internally by restart_frame.
The swizzle calls move from decode_sos to decode_frame but remain within the existing decode_frame operation invoked by H0.

reason: The only harness omission in the commit's stable scope is the pre-existing restart_frame path, which H0 omits in both S0 and S1. The new scan_count bookkeeping and relocated swizzling add internal state and branches but no new caller-facing reachability or control requirement. Under the fixed rule, before=true and after=true with no concrete aggravation is UNCHANGED, so maintenance is not needed.
